papers.title: From business intelligence to conservation intelligence: Operationalizing adaptive pest control of crown‐of‐thorns starfish to protect the resilience of the Great Barrier Reef
papers.authors: Samuel A. Matthews, Roger Beeden, Mary C. Bonin, Camille Mellin, Morgan Stuart Pratchett
papers.abstract: Abstract Resilience‐based management (RBM)—which focuses explicitly on preserving and actively enhancing an ecosystem's capacity to resist and recover from cumulative disturbances under climate change—is crucial for enhancing outcomes in conservation interventions as the climate changes. To be effective it requires continuous modeling, assessment, evaluation and adjustment. Here, we deploy enterprise Business Intelligence software for the purpose of conservation (i.e., Conservation Intelligence) to provide the near real‐time analytics and decision support system necessary for effective RBM. This approach is demonstrated using the Crown‐of‐Thorns Starfish Control Program on Australia's Great Barrier Reef where integrated visual dashboards were developed to assess outbreak severity, prioritize control actions, evaluate effectiveness and incorporate emerging research to close the research‐implementation gap. The flexibility of Business Intelligence software allows these Conservation Intelligence tools to be built and maintained “in‐house,” meeting the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority's (GBRMPA) explicit needs and reducing dependency on external developers or researchers. papers.title: An IHS-ARIMAX Framework for Modeling Cnaphalocrocis medinalis with Potential Implications for Sustainable Pest Management in Rice Fields
papers.authors: Chunyu Jie, Yanhui Lu, Tian JunCe, Yao Wu, Xiaowei Liu
papers.abstract: The rice leaffolder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis) is a major migratory pest whose population dynamics are synergistically driven by endogenous biological factors and exogenous meteorological conditions. Developing precise quantification models for its occurrence is a prerequisite for sustainable pest management. This study applied the Inverse Hyperbolic Sine (IHS) transformation to handle non-normally distributed pest population data with five years of continuous monitoring (2020–2024). We construct two dynamic predictive models: a simplified early warning model (Model I) and a multi-factor coupling model (Model II) by employing the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model with exogenous variables (ARIMAX) to integrate exogenous meteorological drivers (rainfall level during the monitoring interval, Rlt–1,2), endogenous biological indicator (local population development abundance index, LPDAI), and endogenous population dynamic factor (IHS-transformed daily average trap catch increment of the previous interval, IHS_IIPTn–1). papers.title: Evaluation of Gallery Injection for Management of Invasive Shothole Borers ( Euwallacea spp.) Associated with Fusarium Dieback in High-Value Trees
papers.authors: Beatriz E. Nobua-Behrmann, John N. Kabashima
papers.abstract: Abstract Invasive shothole borers ( Euwallacea spp.)(ISHB) and their associated fungal pathogens cause substantial damage to urban and riparian trees, creating a need for diverse management approaches to accommodate different infestation scenarios. Gallery injection, a technique in which small volumes of pesticide are delivered directly into active beetle galleries, has not previously been evaluated for ISHB and may provide a localized treatment option that limits pesticide applications to infested portions of the host. The objective of this study was to evaluate gallery injection as a management approach for ISHB, compare the efficacy of different active ingredients delivered using this method, and quantify the volume of solution that could be delivered into active galleries under field conditions. Field trials were conducted on Platanus spp. in Southern California. Active galleries were verified prior to treatment, and beetle activity was assessed following injections. Gallery injections with emamectin benzoate and imidacloprid significantly reduced gallery activity relative to untreated controls, whereas acephate provided intermediate control. papers.authors: Faith Boa
papers.abstract: The emerald ash borer (EAB) (Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire) is an invasive wood- boring beetle from Asia that primarily feeds on ash trees (Fraxinus spp.). Since its invasion of North America, EAB threatens the functional extinction of ash with damages and management costs projected to reach $900 million by 2054. Current management strategies have been insufficient to prevent EAB’s spread, highlighting the need to advance innovative approaches like RNAi, which has demonstrated efficacy against EAB in laboratory and greenhouse trials. Double-stranded RNA targeting heat shock 70-kDa protein (hsp) induces EAB mortality, systematically disperses and persists in planta, and causes no phenotypic effects for several ash-associated insects. We evaluated the environmental and nontarget effects of dsHSP, focusing on soil communities. In laboratory soil incubation assays, dsHSP was recovered up to 8 h post-treatment. Exposure of the collembolan Folsomia candida to dsHSP-treated soil had no effects on adult survival or body length, but increased reproduction. papers.title: Development of a village health worker care model to reduce cardiovascular risk in areas of armed conflict: Qualitative results from a participatory planning process in Myanmar
papers.authors: Eindra Htoo, Parveen Kaur Parmar, Adam Richards, Tara Russell, Catherine Lee
papers.abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in Myanmar, but care models are lacking to deliver evidence-based treatments to reduce CVD risks in areas of armed conflict. Village health workers (VHWs) play a key role in bridging communities and clinics, but their role in CVD prevention and management in conflict-affected settings has not been clearly defined. This study aimed to identify the functions of VHWs that could improve access and quality of CVD care in conflict-affected areas of Karen State, Myanmar. We conducted 33 key informant interviews with patients, VHWs, clinic staff, ethnic health organization leaders, donors, and non-government organization health experts. A qualitative content analysis was carried out to explore barriers, facilitators, and potential leverage points for improving CVD care in conflict-affected settings. Participants reported that many people were unaware of CVD and its risks, and there were persistent gaps in CVD screening, medication adherence, and referral systems. Transportation costs and hazards, medicine shortages, and security risks made it difficult for patients to visit clinics or achieve continuity of care. Respondent

papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Wildfire and Fuel Treatments in Utah: A Practical Guide and Outcomes From an Oak-Maple Ecosystem
papers.authors: Annie E. Prescott
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. papers.title: Leakage-audited cross-dataset evaluation reveals large generalization gaps in deep learning models for apple and maize disease recognition
papers.authors: Yogesh ., P Sudir, Princy Randhawa, Muzameel Ahmed, B M Chandrakala
papers.abstract: Abstract Deep learning models for plant disease recognition often reach near-perfect accuracy on curated benchmark images, yet how well this performance carries over to independently collected images is rarely measured directly. We trained five image-classification networks (ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet121, ConvNeXt-Tiny and ViT-B/16) on PlantVillage apple and maize leaf images under one shared protocol and tested each trained model, without adaptation, on independently sourced images: 1,730 apple images from Plant Pathology 2020 and 371 web-sourced maize images. Before training, an exact-file audit removed seven duplicate PlantVillage images and found no exact or perceptual near-duplicates shared between source and external datasets. On held-out PlantVillage images, Macro-F1 ranged from 0.949 to 1.000. On external images it fell to 0.472–0.723 for apple and 0.209–0.375 for maize. Exact McNemar tests with Holm correction identified significant differences in per-image correctness for several model pairs. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.authors: Wasswa Shafik, Hassan Tumwiine
papers.abstract: The objective of this chapter is to determine the role of data analytics in enhancing African agricultural supply chains and market access. The specific questions are as follows: What data and analytics are needed to support increased productivity and improved supply chain performance? How does data enable market coordination, farmer bargaining power, and supply-side risk management? And how does support for data-driven agricultural decision-making differ across regions, taking into account varying agricultural systems, structures, and capacities? Addressing Africa’s food security challenge requires increased food production as well as surplus availability in aggregate and across regions, seasons, and commodities. Yet supply responses by farmers, processors, and traders remain muted. Data analytics can help in optimizing supply chains and planning decisions of actors overcoming natural and commercial incentives, enabling structured trading contracts that reduce risk and credit constraints, and aggregating supply through cooperatives and producer organizations. papers.title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
papers.authors: Steven J. Taylor
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Psychology and Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. Findings indicate that AVI outbreaks have been characterized by fear, disgust, and avoidance of poultry products. Many of the other psychological phenomena observed in AVI outbreaks have been documented in past pandemics and other infectious outbreaks: Blame and anger, disease-related avoidance and stigmatization, xenophobia, conspiracy theories, panic buying, and personal stockpiling have all arisen in response to AVI outbreaks. These psychological phenomena may persist and intensify if AVI outbreaks evolve into a pandemic. The lessons learned from COVID-19 can be used to prepare for a possible AVI pandemic. papers.abstract: Background: This research presents a critical analysis of mycotoxins produced by fungi, particularly the Fusarium genus, which is prevalent in cereal-producing regions. Given the global impact of mycotoxins on food safety and animal health, this study addresses an urgent issue in agricultural science. It highlights the various environmental, physical, and biological factors influencing mycotoxin production, providing valuable insights for developing effective management strategies. The study also discusses the health risks associated with specific mycotoxins, such as zearalenone and fumonisins, which have been linked to serious health issues in both animals and humans. Furthermore, it emphasizes the need for ongoing prevention and control programs to mitigate mycotoxin contamination in the food chain. By exploring analytical challenges and proposing future directions for research and policy, this work contributes significantly to the understanding of mycotoxin dynamics in agricultural systems. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.title: Toward climate-resilient date palm agriculture in the United Arab Emirates: a strategic triangulated knowledge mapping
papers.authors: Sajid Safeer, Giuseppe Natale Basile, Sajid Maqsood, Cataldo Pulvento
papers.abstract: The date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) plays a vital role in food security, rural livelihoods, and cultural heritage in the hyper-arid United Arab Emirates (UAE). However, increasing climate stress, water scarcity, and persistent production constraints threaten the sector’s long-term resilience. Addressing these challenges requires a comprehensive understanding of existing research and its limitations. This study systematically maps the thematic structure of UAE date-palm research, identifies dominant knowledge domains, and highlights critical gaps hindering the transition toward climate-resilient and integrated agricultural systems. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, combining bibliometric analysis of 124 peer-reviewed articles (2005–2026) with Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling to identify major thematic clusters. A complementary systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted to validate findings and synthesize emerging research trajectories. papers.abstract: ABSTRACT BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) and chronic latent DNA virus infections frequently reactivate after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), where they contribute to major complications in humans with limited options for prevention or treatment. Mauritian cynomolgus macaques (MCMs; Macaca fascicularis ) serve as an important animal model for transplantation research due to their limited major histocompatibility complex diversity. Similar viral reactivations and disease complications occur in MCMs and humans post-transplantation, including polyomavirus-associated hemorrhagic cystitis and nephropathy. papers.title: TWO PATHS, TWO IDEOLOGIES: ĐORĐE STRATIMIROVIĆ, SVETOZAR MILETIĆ, AND DIVISIONS AMONG THE SERBIAN ELITES IN THE HABSBURG MONARCHY
papers.authors: Горан Васин
papers.source: OpenAlex / ISTRAŽIVANJA Јournal of Historical Researches
papers.abstract: In the 1860s, deep divisions emerged among the Serbian elite in the Habsburg monarchy regarding the optimal political approach for establishing Serbian Vojvodina and creating a more equitable position for Serbs within the monarchy. Đorđe Stratimirović and Svetozar Miletić, each in his own way, attempted to create an approach that would serve as a model for resolving the Serbian question. They both tried to position themselves as a leading voice in Serbian politics within the monarchy. This years-long struggle had serious repercussions for Serbian society within the monarchy. It took much longer to achieve a final resolution, and the dispute eventually led to the tragedy on Tucindan in 1890.

papers.authors: Mehmet Oğuz Yardımcı, Ajay Kulkarni, Trey Ward, Feras A. Batarseh

As these systems increasingly rely on artificial intelligence, controlled agriculture environments use biological inputs such as leaf images for disease detection and yield estimation; amongst other goals. In this work, we propose a unified detection and attribution framework for agricultural cyber-physical systems (namely: AgriVision). Synthetic concealment and fabrication attack scenarios are created using multiple generative adversarial networks (StyleGAN2, StyleGAN3, R3GAN) and diffusion models (Instruct-Pix2Pix, BLIP-Diffusion, DreamShaper-8) across apple, maize, and tomato imagery. papers.abstract: Plants allocate photosynthetically fixed carbon (C) between metabolic needs, biomass production (BP), and non-structural carbon (NSC), a buffer between carbon supply and demand. While conceptual representation of alternative regulatory mechanisms of NSC has advanced significantly in recent decades, quantitative assessments of NSC's contribution to the ecosystem C budget have not been possible. In contrast, C allocation to BP was ∼43% higher in the wet year. Flux-based F NSC (37 ± 84 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) closely matched F NSC estimates from monthly tissue NSC content (65 ± 77 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) during 2024 (Feb-Dec). We conducted a two-year, two-season study in Belgium (2022–2024) directly comparing winter versus spring accessions via field phenotyping, intact-seed NIRS (n=343), and standardized breadmaking (10% wheat-flour substitution). Culture and microscopy of symptomatic stems indicated that ≈75% of winter injuries were abiotic cold shock, not pathogen mediated. papers.authors: Noha K El-Dougdoug, Dom Magistrado, Kayla I. Perry, Sarah M. Short
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aedes aegypti mosquitoes transmit multiple arboviruses, but population suppression through the mass release of sterile or incompatible male mosquitoes can effectively reduce populations. These methods depend on the reliable mass-rearing of healthy, robust males that can successfully mate with wild females. The microbiota is a critical component of the larval diet, and its modulation can dramatically influence life history traits relevant to mass-rearing and male quality. Here, we used axenic (microbe-free), monoxenic (inoculated with Escherichia coli ), and “laboratory community” mosquitoes (inoculated with an undefined microbiota derived from laboratory mosquitoes) to show that longevity was significantly enhanced in axenic and monoxenic males compared to laboratory community males. Moreover, monoxenic males more efficiently obtained mates in non-competitive mating scenarios compared to laboratory community males. However, microbiota treatment had no effect on mating success when males from different treatments competed for a mate. papers.abstract: Abstract Background Averrhoa carambola L. belonging to the family Oxalidaceae of the order Oxalidales, is a commercially valuable fruit tree extensively grown in tropical and subtropical regions. However, its mitochondrial genome remains uncharacterized. Results In this study, we report the first complete assembly and comprehensive characterization of the A. carambola mitochondrial genome, providing an essential genomic resource for evolutionary and functional studies. The assembled mitochondrial genome is a circular, double-stranded DNA molecule of 421,040 bp with a GC content of 44.56%. It contains 39 protein-coding genes and exhibits a pronounced A/T bias in codon usage. We identified 163 simple sequence repeats (SSRs), 448 long repetitive sequences (≥ 30 bp), and 32 chloroplast-derived DNA fragments. C-to-U RNA editing was the predominant type, with 567 predicted editing sites, mainly concentrated in the nad4 gene. Comparative collinearity analysis revealed extensive structural rearrangements relative to related species, and phylogenomic analysis robustly placed A. carambola within the order Oxalidales. papers.abstract: Abstract Background Date palm ( Phoenix dactylifera L.) sustains oasis livelihoods through farming systems in which clonal propagation coexists with the retention of seed-derived palms. Documenting this diversity requires attention to how farmers name, distinguish and manage their palms. In south-western Algeria, long exposed to Bayoud disease, no inventory of the local varietal repertoire has been published for Taghit since 1985, to our knowledge. This study examined date palm diversity and farmers’ knowledge and practices in the Taghit oasis system, characterised fruit and seed variation among locally recognised varieties, and assessed changes in the repertoire over four decades. Methods Semi-structured interviews with 70 farmers across 39 palm groves in six localities documented varietal names, cultivation practices, knowledge transmission, uses and perceived constraints, including resistance to Bayoud. We analysed varietal frequency, salience and spatial distribution, and compared the repertoire with a 1985 inventory. papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Mosquitoes harbor diverse eukaryotic viruses. These viral communities, or viromes, probably influence mosquito physiology, including pathogen transmission. However, the factors shaping the virome remain largely unstudied, limiting our understanding of its role in mosquito biology. Here, we assess the influence of sex on the eukaryotic virome of mosquitoes. papers.abstract: Survival analysis is critical for cancer prognosis and treatment planning, yet existing methods lack the transparency essential for clinical adoption. While recent pathology agents have demonstrated explainability in diagnostic tasks, they face three limitations for survival prediction: inability to integrate multimodal data, ineffective region-of-interest exploration, and failure to leverage experiential learning from historical cases. We introduce SurvAgent, the first hierarchical chain-of-thought (CoT)-enhanced multi-agent system for multimodal survival prediction. The putative causal agent, here termed the VSD‐associated Ceratobasidiaceae lineage ( Csp ), presents diagnostic challenges due to its fastidious growth requirements and vascular colonization pattern. papers.abstract: Biofilms are spatially structured microbial communities whose architecture, chemistry, mechanics, and cellular states evolve over time. Bulk assays and two-dimensional projections remain useful but cannot resolve how these properties vary with depth or during growth, treatment, dispersal, and regrowth. papers.abstract: Referring Camouflaged Object Detection (Ref-COD) requires segmenting hidden targets guided by reference cues. While supervised methods are annotation-heavy and training-free approaches via sparse point-prompting are sensitive to localization errors, we propose GFR-SAM, a robust three-stage training-free framework. Finally, a Geometric-Semantic Refinement module synergizes bounding box and text prompts to recover fine-grained boundaries and enhance instance recall. Evaluated on the R2C7K benchmark, GFR-SAM outperforms existing training-free methods by 8.7\% in weighted F-measure ($F_β^w$) and competes with supervised state-of-the-art counterparts. papers.abstract: This study is the first to characterize the culturable bacterial diversity within a Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) for sole farming (Solea senegalensis) in Portugal, providing a comprehensive insight into its complex bacterial dynamics. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that Pseudomonadota (76.4%) was the most abundant phylum, followed by Actinomycetota (10.7%) and Bacteroidota (9.8%). At the class level, Gammaproteobacteria (65.7%) and Actinomycetes (10.7%) dominated, with Alteromonadales (33.9%) and Vibrionales (13.7%) as the prevalent orders. A total of 48 bacterial genera were identified, with 34 exclusives to the RAS and 8 exclusives to its water supply. Our findings highlight the presence of bacteria with biotechnological potential, including groups previously identified as probiotics, those with antimicrobial properties, and others involved in bioremediation. papers.authors: Daoyuan Jin, Daniel J Petti, Xue-hai Zhou, Glen C. Rains, Glen C. Rains
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence-based agents are emerging as a transformative paradigm for agriculture, enabling autonomous perception, reasoning, decision-making, and coordinated action across complex data and operational environments. These systems could improve productivity, resilience, resource efficiency, and food security, while raising challenges related to robustness, interoperability, data governance, trust, equity, and regulation. This Review examines the rise of these systems in agriculture and outlines research priorities for their development and deployment.

papers.title: Beyond chemical miticides: new frontiers against emerging genetic resistance in Varroa destructor mites in Australia
papers.authors: Lucy Miles, Roy Barkan, Robert J. Harvey, Kate E. Mounsey
papers.abstract: Varroa destructor mites parasitize Western and Eastern honey bees ( Apis mellifera and Apis cerana ) and drive significant colony losses worldwide. In Australia, the recent widespread establishment of Varroa threatens a A$14 billion (~US$10 billion) per annum honey bee industry and agricultural pollination services. Current synthetic miticides used to combat Varroa often target neurotransmitter receptors and ion channels, including pyrethroids (flumethrin, τ-fluvalinate) and amitraz. Alarmingly, Varroa with genetic resistance to both pyrethroids and amitraz have recently emerged in Australia. Beekeepers are now increasingly reliant on non-synthetic ‘soft’ miticides, which are often less effective and negatively impact colony health when used in the high temperatures common across much of Australia. New approaches are clearly needed to combat Varroa . One such next-generation technology is RNA interference (RNAi), in which double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) silences essential genes. RNAi can achieve high species specificity, has a more favorable human and environmental safety profile when appropriately designed, and is less susceptible to genetic resistance caused by target site alteration

papers.title: ZmSGT1‐mediated competitive protection of ZmBBI1 enhances maize resistance to Rhizoctonia solani
papers.authors: Yuanyuan Sun, Le Wang, Xiaofei He, Bingding Zhu, Zhijin Ma
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Integrative Plant Biology
papers.abstract: Banded leaf and sheath blight (BLSB), incited by the necrotrophic basidiomycete Rhizoctonia solani, is a devastating soil-borne disease that severely constrains global maize (Zea mays) production. Bowman-Birk inhibitors (BBIs) constitute a critical class of protease inhibitors in plant innate immunity; yet, their biological functions and upstream regulatory circuits in maize defense against necrotrophic pathogens remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we show that ZmBBI1, a BBI family member transcriptionally upregulated upon R. solani infection, positively modulates BLSB resistance. Its defense activity is strictly dependent on trypsin-inhibitory function, mediated by the evolutionarily conserved Thr52 and Arg53 residues in its canonical reactive loop. We identify Rs03254, a secreted virulence effector from R. solani, that directly engages ZmBBI1 and biochemically inactivates its protease-inhibitory activity to promote fungal colonization. We further demonstrate that the conserved immune co-chaperone ZmSGT1 physically interacts with ZmBBI1 and is genetically required for its full defense function. papers.title: Can omnivores be considered keystone species? Bears as a study case
papers.authors: Grégoire Pauly, Cécile Vanpé, Mélanie Roy, Pierre‐Yves Quenette, Tanguy Daufresne
papers.abstract: Abstract The functional roles of herbivores and carnivores in ecosystems have been relatively well studied: both can shape ecosystems through strong direct and indirect top‐down controls on other guilds. By contrast, the role omnivores play has been rarely explored, even though their diet spans several trophic levels and potentially has numerous effects on ecosystems through trophic and non‐trophic interactions. To gain a better understanding of the potential ecosystemic role of omnivore trophic and non‐trophic interactions, we performed a literature review on bears (Ursidae): a specific group of terrestrial omnivores. We submitted equation searches on the Web of Science for each type of interaction and omnivorous bear species. We kept 411 references highlighting a wide range of trophic and non‐trophic interactions in various ecosystems. Our review sheds light on the large number, diversity, and significance of these interactions. Moreover, we highlight a great variability of interactions among bear species but also across ecosystems for a given bear species.
